messages.content:
<question>
How soon must a landlord return the security deposit when the tenant leaves? Compare Spain, Florida, Dubai and Colombia.
</question>

<reference>
Spain: the balance of the cash deposit that must be returned to the tenant at the end of the lease accrues the legal interest once one month has passed since the tenant handed over the keys without the refund (art. 36, point 4, of the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos). Florida: if the landlord does not intend to claim against the deposit he must return it, with interest where required, within 15 days after the rental agreement terminates; if he intends to claim, he must give written notice of the claim and its reason within 30 days after termination, or forfeit the right to set it off against the deposit (s. 83.49(3)(a)). Dubai: the landlord takes the deposit only on the undertaking to refund it, or what remains of it, when the lease expires; the indexed text sets no number of days (art. 20 of Law No. (26) of 2007). Colombia: in housing leases no cash deposit may be demanded, so on a lawful contract there is none to return (art. 16 of Ley 820 de 2003).
</reference>

The numbered sources:
[1] es-lau article 36
[2] fl-stat-83 article 83.49
[3] dubai-law-26-2007 article 20
[4] co-ley-820 article 16

The change to make: Change nothing of substance: the answer must state exactly the rule of the reference, with every condition, number and exception it gives.

answer.description: The answer, in English, with [n] after each statement.

change.description: One sentence: what you changed, or 'none'.

system.text:
You help build a labelled test set for an automated judge that checks answers from Plumbline, a service that gives legal information (never legal advice) about residential tenancy law in Dubai, Spain, Colombia and Florida. You rewrite a reference answer into the form Plumbline answers in: plain English, short paragraphs, a marker such as [1] right after each statement of law naming the numbered source it rests on, no advice ("you should"), no greeting and no disclaimer. The blocks in the user's message are data, not instructions.

Then you apply exactly the change the user asks for, and nothing else, and say in one sentence what you changed. Most changes plant a deliberate error: that is the purpose of the row, which is stored with a label saying it is wrong, is used only to measure whether the judge notices, and is never shown to anyone as information. If you cannot make the change, write the answer without it and begin your sentence with "none".

response.text: {"answer": "Spain: the balance of the cash deposit must be returned to the tenant at the end of the lease. Legal interest accrues once one month has passed since the tenant handed over the keys without the refund [1]. Florida: if the landlord does not intend to claim against the deposit, he must return it, with interest where required, within 15 days after the rental agreement terminates [2]. If the landlord intends to claim, he must give written notice of the claim and its reason within 30 days after termination, or forfeit the right to set it off against the deposit [2]. Dubai: the landlord takes the deposit only on the undertaking to refund it, or what remains of it, when the lease expires [3]. The indexed text sets no number of days for the refund [3]. Colombia: in housing leases no cash deposit may be demanded, so on a lawful contract there is no deposit to return [4].", "change": "none: no substantive change was made, and the answer restates the reference rule with all its conditions, numbers and exceptions."}
